findings.finding: npm test invokes node --test without path boundaries. Extracted/copied future third-party JS tests under AnalyseFuture can enter test discovery; npm workspace membership does not prevent this. ZIP files currently remain compressed and are not discovered as JavaScript tests.
findings.recommendation: Keep references compressed or scope the test command to the maintained component test directories before storing executable reference trees in the checkout.

findings.finding: The adapters validate the initially configured loopback URL but do not set a redirect policy or revalidate redirect destinations. Native fetch follows redirects. The agent also adds a custom session API key header. A redirecting or compromised configured service can therefore undermine the stated endpoint boundary; this was not reproduced in this read-only audit.
findings.recommendation: Before broader use reject redirects or explicitly validate every redirect destination and credential-forwarding rule; test both adapters.

findings.finding: createSession defaults to a local workspace at /workspace; iteration limits and a transport adapter are not execution isolation. The builder does not currently invoke this adapter.
findings.recommendation: Select and verify the restricted workspace strategy before real generated-code execution; do not describe the default as a secure sandbox.

findings.finding: Request URL parsing occurs before the handler try/catch. An invalid absolute URL could reject the async handler outside its error response path; actual HTTP exploitability was not exercised in this audit.
findings.recommendation: In a separately scoped hardening task handle URL parse failures and test malformed request targets.

findings.finding: The local mock is unauthenticated and has no tenant/persistence/rate-limit boundary. It binds loopback by default; changing HOST does not add production controls.
findings.recommendation: Retain local-only operation until reviewed authentication, authorization, quotas and preview isolation exist.
